--- file:///.src/resultMatchToFromResult.ts ---
// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics resultMatchToFromResult:suggestion
import { Effect, Effect as Fx, Exit, Result, Result as R, pipe } from "effect"
import * as ResultModule from "effect/Result"

class ParseError {
  readonly _tag = "ParseError"
  constructor(readonly cause: unknown) {}
}

declare const result: Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const parsePort: (raw: string) => Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const handlers: {
  readonly onFailure: (error: Error) => Effect.Effect<never, Error>
  readonly onSuccess: (value: number) => Effect.Effect<number>
}
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, Error>
declare const fallback: number
const succeed = Effect.succeed
const fail = Effect.fail

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first Result.match with point-free Effect.fail / Effect.succeed.
export const dataFirst = Effect.fromResult(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: the issue example, identity arrows on both handlers and a call as the Result.
export const identityArrows = Result.match(parsePort("8080"), {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: handler order is irrelevant and module aliases are resolved.
export const aliasedModules = R.match(result, {
  onSuccess: (value) => Fx.succeed(value),
  onFailure: (error) => Fx.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: a point-free handler mixed with an identity arrow.
export const mixedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: function(error) {
    return Effect.fail(error)
  },
  onSuccess: (value) => {
    return Effect.succeed(value)
  }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = ResultModule.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the function-pipe form is normalized the same way.
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  result,
  Result.match({
    onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
    onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct data-last application.
export const dataLast = Result.match({
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested inside a generic callback, the lift is still Effect.fromResult.
export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.
export const wrappedFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(new ParseError(error)),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess transforms the value.
export const transformedSuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess ignores its parameter and lifts something else.
export const otherSuccessValue = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (_value) => Effect.succeed(fallback)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type arguments may change the inferred Effect type.
export const explicitTypeArguments = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail<Error | ParseError>(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed<number | string>(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure dies instead of failing.
export const diesOnFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.die,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the failure is recovered into the success channel.
export const recoveredFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the channels are swapped, this is Effect.flip-like, not a lift.
export const swappedChannels = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.fail
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess is lazy rather than an identity lift.
export const lazySuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.sync(() => value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: async handlers return a Promise of an Effect.
export const asyncHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: async (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: async (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Result.fail / Result.succeed rebuild a Result, not an Effect.
export const resultConstructors = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Result.fail,
  onSuccess: Result.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the handlers are not an inline object literal.
export const handlerObject = Result.match(result, handlers)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Exit.match has the same handler names but folds a Cause, not a Result.
export const exitMatch = Exit.match(exit, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

})(result)

export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.
export const wrappedFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(new ParseError(error)),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess transforms the value.
export const transformedSuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess ignores its parameter and lifts something else.
export const otherSuccessValue = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (_value) => Effect.succeed(fallback)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type arguments may change the inferred Effect type.
export const explicitTypeArguments = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail<Error | ParseError>(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed<number | string>(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure dies instead of failing.
export const diesOnFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.die,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the failure is recovered into the success channel.
export const recoveredFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the channels are swapped, this is Effect.flip-like, not a lift.
export const swappedChannels = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.fail
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess is lazy rather than an identity lift.
export const lazySuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.sync(() => value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: async handlers return a Promise of an Effect.
export const asyncHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: async (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: async (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Result.fail / Result.succeed rebuild a Result, not an Effect.
export const resultConstructors = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Result.fail,
  onSuccess: Result.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the handlers are not an inline object literal.
export const handlerObject = Result.match(result, handlers)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Exit.match has the same handler names but folds a Cause, not a Result.
export const exitMatch = Exit.match(exit, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics resultMatchToFromResult:suggestion
import { Effect, Effect as Fx, Exit, Result, Result as R, pipe } from "effect"
import * as ResultModule from "effect/Result"

class ParseError {
  readonly _tag = "ParseError"
  constructor(readonly cause: unknown) {}
}

declare const result: Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const parsePort: (raw: string) => Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const handlers: {
  readonly onFailure: (error: Error) => Effect.Effect<never, Error>
  readonly onSuccess: (value: number) => Effect.Effect<number>
}
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, Error>
declare const fallback: number
const succeed = Effect.succeed
const fail = Effect.fail

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first Result.match with point-free Effect.fail / Effect.succeed.
export const dataFirst = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the issue example, identity arrows on both handlers and a call as the Result.
export const identityArrows = Result.match(parsePort("8080"), {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: handler order is irrelevant and module aliases are resolved.
export const aliasedModules = R.match(result, {
  onSuccess: (value) => Fx.succeed(value),
  onFailure: (error) => Fx.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: a point-free handler mixed with an identity arrow.
export const mixedHandlers = Effect.fromResult(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: function(error) {
    return Effect.fail(error)
  },
  onSuccess: (value) => {
    return Effect.succeed(value)
  }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = ResultModule.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the function-pipe form is normalized the same way.
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  result,
  Result.match({
    onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
    onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct data-last application.
export const dataLast = Result.match({
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested inside a generic callback, the lift is still Effect.fromResult.
export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.

export const mixedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Effect.fromResult(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = ResultModule.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the function-pipe form is normalized the same way.
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  result,
  Result.match({
    onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
    onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct data-last application.
export const dataLast = Result.match({
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested inside a generic callback, the lift is still Effect.fromResult.
export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.
export const wrappedFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(new ParseError(error)),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess transforms the value.
export const transformedSuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess ignores its parameter and lifts something else.
export const otherSuccessValue = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (_value) => Effect.succeed(fallback)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type arguments may change the inferred Effect type.
export const explicitTypeArguments = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail<Error | ParseError>(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed<number | string>(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure dies instead of failing.
export const diesOnFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.die,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the failure is recovered into the success channel.
export const recoveredFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the channels are swapped, this is Effect.flip-like, not a lift.
export const swappedChannels = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.fail
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess is lazy rather than an identity lift.
export const lazySuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.sync(() => value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: async handlers return a Promise of an Effect.
export const asyncHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: async (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: async (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Result.fail / Result.succeed rebuild a Result, not an Effect.
export const resultConstructors = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Result.fail,
  onSuccess: Result.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the handlers are not an inline object literal.
export const handlerObject = Result.match(result, handlers)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Exit.match has the same handler names but folds a Cause, not a Result.
export const exitMatch = Exit.match(exit, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics resultMatchToFromResult:suggestion
import { Effect, Effect as Fx, Exit, Result, Result as R, pipe } from "effect"
import * as ResultModule from "effect/Result"

class ParseError {
  readonly _tag = "ParseError"
  constructor(readonly cause: unknown) {}
}

declare const result: Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const parsePort: (raw: string) => Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const handlers: {
  readonly onFailure: (error: Error) => Effect.Effect<never, Error>
  readonly onSuccess: (value: number) => Effect.Effect<number>
}
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, Error>
declare const fallback: number
const succeed = Effect.succeed
const fail = Effect.fail

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first Result.match with point-free Effect.fail / Effect.succeed.
export const dataFirst = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the issue example, identity arrows on both handlers and a call as the Result.
export const identityArrows = Result.match(parsePort("8080"), {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: handler order is irrelevant and module aliases are resolved.
export const aliasedModules = R.match(result, {
  onSuccess: (value) => Fx.succeed(value),
  onFailure: (error) => Fx.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: a point-free handler mixed with an identity arrow.
export const mixedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: function(error) {
    return Effect.fail(error)
  },
  onSuccess: (value) => {
    return Effect.succeed(value)
  }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = Effect.fromResult(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

    onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
    onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
  })

  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics resultMatchToFromResult:suggestion
import { Effect, Effect as Fx, Exit, Result, Result as R, pipe } from "effect"
import * as ResultModule from "effect/Result"

class ParseError {
  readonly _tag = "ParseError"
  constructor(readonly cause: unknown) {}
}

declare const result: Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const parsePort: (raw: string) => Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const handlers: {
  readonly onFailure: (error: Error) => Effect.Effect<never, Error>
  readonly onSuccess: (value: number) => Effect.Effect<number>
}
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, Error>
declare const fallback: number
const succeed = Effect.succeed
const fail = Effect.fail

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first Result.match with point-free Effect.fail / Effect.succeed.
export const dataFirst = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the issue example, identity arrows on both handlers and a call as the Result.
export const identityArrows = Result.match(parsePort("8080"), {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: handler order is irrelevant and module aliases are resolved.
export const aliasedModules = R.match(result, {
  onSuccess: (value) => Fx.succeed(value),
  onFailure: (error) => Fx.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: a point-free handler mixed with an identity arrow.
export const mixedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: function(error) {
    return Effect.fail(error)
  },
  onSuccess: (value) => {
    return Effect.succeed(value)
  }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = ResultModule.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the function-pipe form is normalized the same way.
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  result,
  Effect.fromResult
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct data-last application.
export const dataLast = Result.match({
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested inside a generic callback, the lift is still Effect.fromResult.
export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.
export const wrappedFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(new ParseError(error)),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess transforms the value.
export const transformedSuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess ignores its parameter and lifts something else.
export const otherSuccessValue = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (_value) => Effect.succeed(fallback)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type arguments may change the inferred Effect type.
export const explicitTypeArguments = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail<Error | ParseError>(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed<number | string>(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure dies instead of failing.
export const diesOnFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.die,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the failure is recovered into the success channel.
export const recoveredFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the channels are swapped, this is Effect.flip-like, not a lift.
export const swappedChannels = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.fail
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess is lazy rather than an identity lift.
export const lazySuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.sync(() => value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: async handlers return a Promise of an Effect.
export const asyncHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: async (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: async (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Result.fail / Result.succeed rebuild a Result, not an Effect.
export const resultConstructors = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Result.fail,
  onSuccess: Result.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the handlers are not an inline object literal.
export const handlerObject = Result.match(result, handlers)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Exit.match has the same handler names but folds a Cause, not a Result.
export const exitMatch = Exit.match(exit, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// @effect-diagnostics *:off
// @effect-diagnostics resultMatchToFromResult:suggestion
import { Effect, Effect as Fx, Exit, Result, Result as R, pipe } from "effect"
import * as ResultModule from "effect/Result"

class ParseError {
  readonly _tag = "ParseError"
  constructor(readonly cause: unknown) {}
}

declare const result: Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const parsePort: (raw: string) => Result.Result<number, Error>
declare const handlers: {
  readonly onFailure: (error: Error) => Effect.Effect<never, Error>
  readonly onSuccess: (value: number) => Effect.Effect<number>
}
declare const exit: Exit.Exit<number, Error>
declare const fallback: number
const succeed = Effect.succeed
const fail = Effect.fail

// MUST TRIGGER: data-first Result.match with point-free Effect.fail / Effect.succeed.
export const dataFirst = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: the issue example, identity arrows on both handlers and a call as the Result.
export const identityArrows = Result.match(parsePort("8080"), {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: handler order is irrelevant and module aliases are resolved.
export const aliasedModules = R.match(result, {
  onSuccess: (value) => Fx.succeed(value),
  onFailure: (error) => Fx.fail(error)
})

// MUST TRIGGER: a point-free handler mixed with an identity arrow.
export const mixedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: local aliases of Effect.succeed / Effect.fail still resolve to the Effect module.
export const handlerAliases = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: fail,
  onSuccess: succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: single-return block bodies and function expressions are still identity lifts.
export const blockBodies = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: function(error) {
    return Effect.fail(error)
  },
  onSuccess: (value) => {
    return Effect.succeed(value)
  }
})

// MUST TRIGGER: Result.match imported through the effect/Result subpath namespace.
export const subpathImport = ResultModule.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST TRIGGER: pipeable Result.match rewrites to result.pipe(Effect.fromResult).
export const pipeable = result.pipe(
  Result.match({
    onFailure: Effect.fail,
    onSuccess: Effect.succeed
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: the function-pipe form is normalized the same way.
export const functionPipe = pipe(
  result,
  Result.match({
    onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(error),
    onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
  })
)

// MUST TRIGGER: direct data-last application.
export const dataLast = Result.match({
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: nested inside a generic callback, the lift is still Effect.fromResult.
export const nested = <A, E>(effect: Effect.Effect<Result.Result<A, E>>) =>
  Effect.flatMap(effect, (inner) =>
    Result.match(inner, {
      onFailure: Effect.fail,
      onSuccess: Effect.succeed
    }))

// MUST TRIGGER: isSuccess guard ternary reading .success / .failure from the tested identifier.
export const isSuccessTernary = Effect.fromResult(result)

// MUST TRIGGER: isFailure guard ternary mirrors the branch roles.
export const isFailureTernary = R.isFailure(result)
  ? Fx.fail(result.failure)
  : Fx.succeed(result.success)

// MUST TRIGGER: guard ternary on a parameter inside a function.
export const ternaryInFunction = (parsed: Result.Result<string, ParseError>) =>
  Result.isSuccess(parsed) ? Effect.succeed(parsed.success) : Effect.fail(parsed.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the SchemaGetter near-miss, onFailure builds a new error instead of lifting it.
export const rewrappedFailureThunk = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: () => Effect.fail(new ParseError("invalid")),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure wraps the original error.
export const wrappedFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail(new ParseError(error)),
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess transforms the value.
export const transformedSuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed(value + 1)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess ignores its parameter and lifts something else.
export const otherSuccessValue = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (_value) => Effect.succeed(fallback)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: explicit type arguments may change the inferred Effect type.
export const explicitTypeArguments = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: (error) => Effect.fail<Error | ParseError>(error),
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.succeed<number | string>(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onFailure dies instead of failing.
export const diesOnFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.die,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the failure is recovered into the success channel.
export const recoveredFailure = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the channels are swapped, this is Effect.flip-like, not a lift.
export const swappedChannels = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.succeed,
  onSuccess: Effect.fail
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: onSuccess is lazy rather than an identity lift.
export const lazySuccess = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: (value) => Effect.sync(() => value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: async handlers return a Promise of an Effect.
export const asyncHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: async (error) => Effect.fail(error),
  onSuccess: async (value) => Effect.succeed(value)
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Result.fail / Result.succeed rebuild a Result, not an Effect.
export const resultConstructors = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: Result.fail,
  onSuccess: Result.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the handlers are not an inline object literal.
export const handlerObject = Result.match(result, handlers)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Exit.match has the same handler names but folds a Cause, not a Result.
export const exitMatch = Exit.match(exit, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: Effect.match folds an Effect, it is not Result.match.
export const effectMatch = Effect.match(Effect.succeed(1), {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

const local = {
  succeed: <A>(value: A) => Effect.succeed(value),
  fail: <E>(error: E) => Effect.fail(error),
  match: <A, E, B, C>(
    value: Result.Result<A, E>,
    options: { readonly onFailure: (error: E) => B; readonly onSuccess: (value: A) => C }
  ): B | C => Result.isSuccess(value) ? options.onSuccess(value.success) : options.onFailure(value.failure)
}

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: an unrelated match with the same surface shape.
export const unrelatedMatch = local.match(result, {
  onFailure: Effect.fail,
  onSuccess: Effect.succeed
})

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: same-named succeed / fail that are not the Effect module APIs.
export const unrelatedHandlers = Result.match(result, {
  onFailure: local.fail,
  onSuccess: local.succeed
})

declare const otherSuccess: Result.Success<number, Error>
declare const otherFailure: Result.Failure<number, Error>
declare const holder: { readonly result: Result.Result<number, Error> }

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the succeed branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedSuccess = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(otherSuccess.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the fail branch reads a different Result than the one tested.
export const mismatchedFailure = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(otherFailure.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the failure.
export const transformedTernary = Result.isSuccess(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(new ParseError(result.failure))

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard ternary transforms the success value.
export const transformedTernarySuccess = Result.isFailure(result)
  ? Effect.fail(result.failure)
  : Effect.succeed(result.success * 2)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the tested Result is a property access, not a plain identifier.
export const propertyAccessTernary = Result.isSuccess(holder.result)
  ? Effect.succeed(holder.result.success)
  : Effect.fail(holder.result.failure)

// MUST NOT TRIGGER: the guard is not the Effect Result module's isSuccess.
export const unrelatedGuard = ((value: Result.Result<number, Error>): value is Result.Success<number, Error> =>
    value._tag === "Success")(result)
  ? Effect.succeed(result.success)
  : Effect.fail(result.failure)
